- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to underpredict sharp upward moves; adjust forecast upward by 2–5% for the next 3–5 days.
- After a spike in price (e.g., >85), model often overreacts and forecasts continued steep rise; cap forecast at +5% above peak or apply mean reversion to 10–15 day moving average.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive mid-period, model delays reaction; forecast should begin rising 1–2 days earlier than model suggests.
- Model frequently underestimates late-period volatility (especially after 15–20 days); add 1–3% buffer to final 5–7 days of forecast.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral, model tends to average out; use sentiment-weighted median of recent 5–7 days to anchor forecast mid-range.
- If model forecast is below 75 and sentiment is positive, consider upward bias correction; if above 85 and sentiment negative, apply downward cap.
